outcome: No event dated after 26 January 2024 bearing on the largest pathwidth of an n-vertex cubic graph was found in any source I could reach. The bounds in circulation are unchanged: an upper bound of (1/6 + ε)n for large n, from Fomin and Høie (2006), and a best known lower bound of 0.082n, attributed by Wikipedia to Fomin and Høie (2006) but traced by one search snippet to Bezrukov et al. (2000) via bisection width. The only later paper on cubic-graph pathwidth I could read (Bachtler and Heinrich, arXiv 2020, JGT 2024) proves girth-based bounds that cannot move either constant.
problem_asks: The largest possible pathwidth of an n-vertex cubic graph. Part 1: for each n, M(n) = max{ pathwidth(G) : G a cubic graph on n vertices }, i.e. the exact value or closed form of M(n) for every n. Part 2 (implicit in asking for the scale of M(n)): the limiting constant c = lim M(n)/n, if the limit exists. The statement asks for an exact maximum and does not state any bound; it does not ask about graphs of maximum degree 3 in general, nor about other width parameters (treewidth, cutwidth, bisection width), though the cited upper bound covers max-degree-3 graphs.

events.what_happened: Fomin and Høie, 'Pathwidth of cubic graphs and exact algorithms', Information Processing Letters 97(5), pp. 191-196 (DOI 10.1016/j.ipl.2005.10.012). Per search-engine snippets quoting the abstract (the paper itself was not readable), for every ε > 0 there is an integer n_ε such that every cubic (3-regular) graph on n > n_ε vertices has pathwidth at most (1/6 + ε)n; the snippet states the theorem also holds for graphs of maximum degree 3. Wikipedia's 'Cubic graph' and 'Pathwidth' articles cite this paper for the upper bound (stated as n/6, and as n/6 + o(n) in the Pathwidth article) and for the lower bound 0.082n ('there exist cubic graphs with pathwidth 0.082n'). The paper is used to give O*(2^(n/6)) exact algorithms for maximum independent set and related problems.
events.revisions: None found. IPL volume 97 issue 5 (2006). The DOI suffix suggests acceptance or online posting in late 2005; the PDF metadata reads January 2006. The month of first public posting was not established, so only the year is recorded.
events.delivers: Upper bound: pathwidth at most (1/6 + ε)n for every cubic graph on more than n_ε vertices, for every fixed ε > 0 (quoted from the abstract in a search snippet; not read in full). Per Wikipedia, also a lower bound: some cubic graphs have pathwidth 0.082n. It gives no exact value of M(n) and no exact asymptotic constant.
events.remains: The exact value of M(n) for every n. The constant c = lim M(n)/n, which the cited results place in [0.082, 1/6]. Small-n values are not given.

events.what_happened: Bezrukov, Elsässer, Monien, Preis and Tillich, 'New spectral lower bounds on the bisection width of graphs', WG 2000 (LNCS 1928, pp. 23-34), journal version Theoretical Computer Science 320 (2004) 155-174 (DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2004.03.059). A secondary citation (Lichev and Mitsche, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 30(2), 2023, seen only as a search snippet) says the paper gives a lower bound of 0.082n on the bisection width of 3-regular Ramanujan graphs. A search snippet states that the 2006 Fomin and Høie paper uses this result to get the pathwidth lower bound 0.082n; I could not confirm that transfer in any primary text.
events.revisions: Conference version WG 2000; journal version TCS 2004. The sources give no month.
events.delivers: As far as I could verify: a lower bound on the bisection width (not the pathwidth) of 3-regular Ramanujan graphs, reported as 0.082n by a secondary source. Whether this yields a pathwidth lower bound of 0.082n for cubic graphs is unverified; it is asserted only in a search snippet.
events.remains: The maximum pathwidth of cubic graphs, the whole of M(n). No pathwidth statement from this paper was verified.

events.doubts: The source of the 0.082n figure for cubic-graph pathwidth is contested (see disputes). The bisection-to-pathwidth transfer is asserted only in a search snippet; I could not check it.
events.direction: Lower bound on a neighbouring quantity (bisection width of 3-regular Ramanujan graphs). If the transfer to pathwidth holds, it would be a lower bound 0.082n on M(n), which is the figure Wikipedia attributes to Fomin and Høie.

events.what_happened: Bachtler and Heinrich, 'Automated testing and interactive construction of unavoidable sets for graph classes of small path-width', arXiv:2010.08373 (v1, 16 October 2020; only v1 is listed on the arXiv abstract page). Published in the Journal of Graph Theory 104(2), pp. 289-319 (TU Darmstadt repository deposit dated 9 February 2024; sources give the issue year as 2023 and as 2024). The main results, read in the arXiv text (ar5iv HTML): Theorem 1.1, for every k >= 3, the largest girth ξ(k) of a cubic graph of pathwidth k satisfies ξ(k) <= (2/3)k + 10/3; Theorem 1.2, ξ(k) <= k - 2 for k >= 10. The paper also computes the extremal girth values for pathwidth 3 to 10 and characterises the extremal cubic graphs of pathwidth 3 and girth 4, using a computer framework.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (16 Oct 2020). JGT 104(2), 289-319, deposited 9 Feb 2024. I read only the arXiv text; the journal text may differ from v1 and was not read.
events.delivers: Girth-based bounds only. A cubic graph of girth g has pathwidth at least (3g - 10)/2 by Theorem 1.1, and at least g + 2 when its pathwidth is at least 10 by Theorem 1.2. These bound pathwidth below in terms of girth. They do not give a lower bound on M(n) as a function of n with a linear constant. With n-vertex cubic graphs of girth Θ(log n) they give M(n) = Ω(log n) at most (my derivation, not stated in the paper), well below 0.082n.
events.remains: All of M(n): the paper gives no bound on the largest pathwidth of n-vertex cubic graphs, and no scaling constant for it.

disputes.summary: The 0.082n lower bound on the pathwidth of cubic graphs. Wikipedia's Cubic graph and Pathwidth articles credit Fomin and Høie (2006). A search snippet credits the number to Bezrukov et al. (WG 2000 / TCS 2004), with Fomin and Høie passing it to pathwidth. A second snippet, citing Lichev and Mitsche (2023), attributes the 0.082n figure to Bezrukov et al. for bisection width of 3-regular Ramanujan graphs. Kozma (arXiv 1902.08809, 2019) gives the range 0.082n to 0.167n without naming a source in the snippet. The primary texts that would settle this were not readable.

Search summaries describe Bachtler and Heinrich as proving 'a new lower bound on the path-width of cubic graphs' that could bear on the 0.082n floor. The arXiv text read (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, ar5iv HTML) states girth-versus-pathwidth bounds only and gives no linear lower bound in n. The journal version was not read, so a difference between versions is not excluded.

summary: I ran 40 web searches and opened the main primary and secondary pages I could reach: Wikipedia's Cubic graph, Pathwidth and List of unsolved problems in mathematics (the entry sits under Graph theory, Subgraphs, citing [133], whose text I could not reach), the arXiv abstract and ar5iv text of Bachtler and Heinrich, the arXiv abstracts of Baste et al. excluded items, and the GitHub graph-conjecture repository and catalogue. The searches covered the problem name and variants, the bound-language, post-2006 improvements, the Bezrukov source, exact small-order computation, and separate AI queries. No event dated after 26 January 2024 bearing on M(n) was found. The known bounds are the Fomin and Høie (2006) upper bound of (1/6 + ε)n for large n (Wikipedia gives n/6 + o(n)), and a lower bound of 0.082n. The primary Fomin and Høie text could not be read: every copy returned binary, a 403, or a bot-block. Both bounds therefore rest on Wikipedia citations and on search-snippet quotes of the abstract. The attribution of 0.082n is contested (disputes). The Bezrukov et al. (2000) bisection-width result, reported by a secondary citation as 0.082n for 3-regular Ramanujan graphs, is recorded as an event. Its transfer to pathwidth is unverified. The Bachtler and Heinrich arXiv paper (2020; JGT 2024) is recorded as a discarded event: its theorems are girth-versus-pathwidth bounds (Theorem 1.1: girth at most 2k/3 + 10/3 when pathwidth is k; Theorem 1.2: girth at most k - 2 for k >= 10), which cannot yield a linear lower bound in n, since cubic girth is O(log n). Its finite extremal tables are not a bound on M(n). On AI involvement: no AI system is credited with any result on this quantity, and none of the AI-credited results I found touches it. The GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra cycle double cover proof (July 2026, reported as reducing the conjecture to cubic graphs) has no pathwidth step visible in any report I read; its PDF was not opened. The row pathwidth of complete binary trees (arXiv 2608.09495, AI-use statement crediting GPT-5.6 Sol Pro) concerns a different parameter; I saw its statement in a snippet only. AlphaProof Nexus (arXiv 2605.22763) and the Claude Fable 5 Jacobian report concern other problems. The graph-theory-AI catalogue and repository, read through summarising fetches, contain no pathwidth or cubic-pathwidth row. Lean/mathlib searches found no formalisation of a pathwidth bound for cubic graphs. Dead ends are listed in search.dead_ends.
competing_reading: A reader who takes the search summaries at face value could read Bachtler and Heinrich as a new lower bound on the pathwidth of cubic graphs that improves the 0.082n floor. The arXiv theorems show it is a girth statement and cannot reach linear order in n. A reader who trusts Wikipedia's attribution would count the 0.082n figure as part of the 2006 Fomin and Høie event; a reader who trusts the snippet would place it under Bezrukov et al. (2000). Whichever is right, none of these readings puts a post-2024 event on this problem, so the window answer is the same.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full Fomin and Høie (2006) text: the exact theorem, its constant and hypotheses, and whether the 0.082n lower bound is theirs or quoted from Bezrukov et al. (2) The Bezrukov et al. TCS 2004 paper, for any pathwidth remark or transfer. (3) The full JGT 2024 text of Bachtler and Heinrich, for any lower bound on M(n) of linear order that the arXiv version lacks. (4) A citation search (Google Scholar or Semantic Scholar, both blocked from here) for 2024-2026 papers citing Fomin and Høie (2006) with a changed constant or a computed M(n) for small n. (5) Reference [133] in the Wikipedia list's references section, which the list entry cites.

events.credibility_reason: The paper's verified content is a bisection-width bound for 3-regular Ramanujan graphs; its transfer to a 0.082n pathwidth lower bound rests only on a search snippet, and the attribution is disputed.

judgement.why: All three events are dated before 26 January 2024. Fomin–Høie (2006) and Bezrukov et al. (2000, conference version) are pre-snapshot by year. Bachtler–Heinrich's first public argument is arXiv v1 of October 2020, and the 2024 JGT deposit shows no new mathematics (F1). Fomin–Høie bounds M(n) above by (1/6+ε)n and leaves the quantity open, so it is a bound published in a journal of record. Bezrukov et al. bound bisection width. That gives a pathwidth lower bound only through a transfer that the record could not confirm, so I score it a bound and mark it doubtful. Bachtler–Heinrich relates girth to pathwidth and does not move M(n) as a function of n, so its scope is none. Its finite extremal tables are not witnesses for the statement. No event involves AI. No pre-snapshot event resolves the question either.
judgement.doubts: Neither primary text for Fomin–Høie nor for Bezrukov et al. was read. The exact constants and the attribution of 0.082n rest on Wikipedia and on search snippets. The post-2024 citation search could not be run, so a later improvement in a paper that does not use the problem's wording could have been missed.
